objective: Verify that a Paper Out/Export package's Media Type is derived from what the requester (UI user or API integrator) actually declares - not from the submission channel alone - that the acknowledgement flow for Save as Electronic File behaves as specified, that the mediaType element is correctly optional on eoRequestExport, that Media Type is logged on the Submitted Paper Out event and never backfilled retroactively, and that the two small UI text/layout fixes ship. Each scenario asserts only what its approved acceptance criterion asserts.

inScope: Media Type for Paper Out Package section on the Paper Out Request modal (AC-EC-12000-001).
Acknowledgement modal behavior for Save as Electronic File: gated OK, always-enabled Cancel, Work Queue item creation on confirm, no side effect on cancel (AC-EC-12000-002 through -004).
eoRequestExport / export.xsd optional mediaType element and backward compatibility (AC-EC-12000-005, -006).
Media Type determination logic for UI and API paths, at transaction and document level (AC-EC-12000-007 through -015).
Media Type Additional Information logged on Submitted Paper Out, visible on cover page/audit trail/activity history reports, and never backfilled (AC-EC-12000-016, -017).
Verify Paper Out modal checkbox verbiage update (AC-EC-12000-018).
Paper Out Request modal right-side border alignment (AC-EC-12000-019).
Collections-initiated Paper Out reusing the same modal and logic, per AMB-EC-12000-001's resolution (Collections accordion > Batch > Paper Out Request).
outOfScope: Any part of the eoRequestExport / export.xsd contract beyond the new mediaType element - not defined by this story and not authored here.
Retroactive Media Type backfill on historical transactions/documents - explicitly excluded by the story (AC-EC-12000-017 asserts the exclusion itself).

The full authoritative eoRequestExport request/response contract - unresolved as AMB-EC-12000-002 until captured via Playwright MCP at PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION and promoted to HUMAN_APPROVED by a human reviewer.

risks.description: eoRequestExport has no authoritative contract and does not even appear in reports/validation/ecore-api-discovery.json's declaredButNotObserved list, so its request/response shape is completely unverified, not merely unconfirmed.
risks.mitigation: AC-EC-12000-005, -006 and -011 through -015 are declared interfaceType API with apiContract.contractSource UNVERIFIED. They cannot back an assertion until Playwright MCP observation at PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION produces a contract that a human promotes to HUMAN_APPROVED with a recorded responseShapeHash. No endpoint path or status code is guessed.

risks.description: Confirming the acknowledgement modal creates a real Work Queue approval item against shared QA data, which is a write with a downstream effect (an approval workflow item).
risks.mitigation: Only fabricated requester/approver test data is used (never a real business identity); the created Work Queue item is a normal, reversible approval-queue entry rather than a destructive call, and its creation is itself the behavior AC-EC-12000-003 requires being verified.

risks.description: Moving Media Type Additional Information from the Authorized Paper Out event to the Submitted Paper Out event could break any pre-existing automation or report that reads the old event location.
risks.mitigation: AC-EC-12000-016 and -017 assert the new location and the no-retroactive-update rule explicitly, so this is treated as a deliberate, visible behavior change. Any pre-existing automation asserting the old event must be reviewed at IMPLEMENTATION time rather than left silently broken.

risks.description: The Collections entry point's reuse of the same modal (AMB-EC-12000-001) is a human-supplied answer, not yet confirmed against the running application.
risks.mitigation: The Collections navigation path is validated against the real application via Playwright MCP at PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION before automation asserts it as fact.

risks.description: The eoRequestExport endpoint (method, path, content-type and form-part names) was supplied by a human reviewer in chat rather than an independently observed or documented source -- no WSDL, integration guide, or captured network trace corroborates it. Per AGENTS.md rule 4's drafting exception it is recorded as AGENT_DRAFTED with contractSource UNVERIFIED. If the dictated endpoint is wrong, the call may fail safely, or may reach an unintended host/operation with a real side effect, because the request is genuinely issued rather than merely observed.
risks.mitigation: TS-EC-12000-011 through -015 remain scaffoldingOnly: true; Media Type continues to be asserted exclusively via the UI audit trail (CLR-TP-EC-12000-001), never via the API response, so a wrong or malformed response cannot produce a false pass. expectedStatusCodes=[200] is PROPOSED only and does not gate the acceptance criterion.

risks.description: eoRequestExport is destructive-by-name (its own request schema carries deleteIfEmpty and irreversible retentionPolicy attributes) and would now be called for real, against the shared qa5 fixture, by TS-EC-12000-011 through -015 -- in addition to the eight UI-driven Submit+Cancel scenarios (TS-EC-12000-003, -007 through -010, -016) already approved in v1/v2 against the same single qualifying fixture collection.
risks.mitigation: CLEANUP mechanism confirmed at Gate 2 (reviewer Anil, 2026-09-15) and observed live against qa5: Print the Work Queue item, select all in the Verify Paper Out modal, click Verify, confirm the alert -- this clears the item from the Work Queue (mirrors the existing MANUAL_ONLY flow documented in TS-EC-12000-020). Fixtures must be selected dynamically from the currently available Collections list at run time (never a hard-coded id), reducing contention with the eight already-approved UI scenarios sharing the same pool.

clarifications.question: Does a Paper Out initiated from Collections use the same Paper Out Request modal, or a separate flow?
Who captures and approves the authoritative eoRequestExport contract before any API-facing criterion can be judged?
Which fields are the required field edits that gate the acknowledgement modal?

TS-EC-12000-005, -006 and -011 through -015 are currently declared API-only with an UNVERIFIED contract (per AMB-EC-12000-002's resolution). Once Playwright MCP observation at PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION produces a contract, should these be promoted straight to HUMAN_APPROVED as pure API scenarios, or does any of them also need a UI-observable assertion (HYBRID) to be fully covered? RESOLVED at Gate 2 (reviewer Anil): TS-005/006 stay pure API (they assert only on the eoRequestExport request/response itself). TS-011 through TS-015 are HYBRID (the API call sets Media Type, but the only currently-confirmed observation channel is the UI audit trail per AC-016), unless PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION later confirms a verified read API exists, at which point this may be revisited.

AC-EC-12000-016 names four surfaces: the Submitted Paper Out event, the Authorized Paper Out event, the package cover page and the downloaded activity history report. Three were confirmed observable and automatable live against qa5 on 2026-09-14. The fourth, the cover page, was not: the package is served by getPrintableDocumentContents.eo, which returns HTML rather than a PDF while the batch is merely Submitted and yields the package only once the batch is Authorized. Authorizing the fixture is a one-way door - a Submitted request can be cancelled, but the only exit after authorization is Verify, which permanently removes the source documents from the vault and would consume the single qa5 collection that qualifies for Paper Out at all. Should the cover-page clause therefore be split into its own MANUAL_ONLY scenario (TS-EC-12000-020), leaving TS-EC-12000-016 to automate the other three surfaces?

TS-EC-12000-017 requires a Paper Out record created BEFORE this change was deployed, so that it can be shown not to have been retroactively given a Media Type. No such record is reachable in qa5: the fixture document and four other collections were scanned on 2026-09-14 and every Submitted Paper Out event carries a Media Type, because all of them originate from this automation run. Note that Canceled Paper Out events legitimately carry no Media Type, so "any event lacking one" is not a safe proxy and would pass for the wrong reason. Which specific pre-deployment transaction or document should this scenario use, or should it be DEFERRED until one is identified?

TS-EC-12000-011 through -015 would now call eoRequestExport for real, using a human-dictated (AGENT_DRAFTED, contractSource UNVERIFIED) endpoint: POST ${ecoreBaseUrl}/ecore/, multipart/form-data with parts action=eoRequestExport and instructionsXML.
